Customer experience and community · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Content from recurring questions

Ruben · Customer Education Specialist

On a B2B platform with 34 lessons in the academy and 210 articles in the help center, 30% of the quarter's tickets deal with eight subjects that have no specific lesson or article.

When it runs
Monthly close of the content queue, in the first business week of each month, with tickets and forum topics from the previous 90 days
What it delivers in production
A monthly proposal with the eight highest-demand topics that lack material and the justification in numbers. For the top three, a lesson script and article draft citing the documentation, ready for teaching review and technical validation.
Who decides
Proposes topic and draft; the instructor decides
Effort
Calibrate on one quarter; first proposal in a month

# Content curation rules (excerpt)

## Prioritization
- Order by total occurrences (tickets + topics). Tie: the topic without material comes first.
- Estimated support cost: tickets in the group x 25 minutes (average time per tier 1 support ticket), in hours and minutes (written "3 h 45 min").
- Proposal: no lesson and no article, short lesson + article; outdated article, update the article; lesson or article less than 60 days old, leave it alone.

## Style guide
- Draft sections: Objective, Prerequisites, Script (timing and [capture]), Supporting article, Check questions.
- Verifiable objective: "by the end, the administrator configures...". Lesson of up to 12 minutes.
- Screen name as the customer sees it, with the path: Settings > Approvals.
- Citation next to the sentence: [doc: product_documentation.md, section Levels].

## Rules with no leeway
- A group qualifies with 15 or more occurrences, adding tickets and topics. E.g.: import with custom columns has 8 + 7 = 15 and qualifies; keyboard shortcuts (1 topic) stays out.
- A ticket in the defect category leaves the topics and goes to the support list. E.g.: PDF export error (3 tickets) is a defect, with no same-day alert (3, below 30).
- Dates against the base date in READ-base-date.txt. E.g.: article reviewed on 2025-08-20 is outdated; lesson published on 2026-10-01 is 33 days old and is not changed.
- Arithmetic: cost = tickets x 25 min. E.g.: 9 x 25 = 225 min = 3 h 45 min.
- A statement with no section in the documentation becomes CONFIRM WITH SPECIALIST, even when it comes from the forum. E.g.: approval by amount range.
- A permissions topic carries the full technical validation mark on the topic line.
- Company, person, e-mail and account data do not appear in any part of the output, not even in the draft example. E.g.: the e-mail and the company of T-108 stay out.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Official product documentation (excerpt)

## Approvals
### Levels
Screen Settings > Approvals > Levels. Up to 3 levels in sequence. Each level has one approver or a group of approvers. Deadline per level from 24 to 72 hours; with no answer within the deadline, the request moves up to the next level.

### Permissions
Only the Administrator profile creates or changes approval rules. The Approver profile only approves or rejects. An Approver does not see requests from other levels.

## Import
### Custom columns
Screen Import > Map columns. Up to 20 custom columns per import, of the types text, number and date. .xlsx or .csv file of up to 10 MB.

### Common errors
A date outside the YYYY-MM-DD format is rejected row by row, with the row number in the error report.

## Reports
### Export
Reports export to PDF and CSV, up to 50 thousand rows.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A statement about the product without a documentation page is removed before review, because wrong training material creates more tickets than no material at all. The Human AI does not record, publish or change existing articles; the instructor decides the teaching approach and the specialist validates the technical content. Topics on permissions, billing or data deletion go through full technical validation even after the supervised phase. A ticket excerpt used as an example loses the company name, user and account data.

Common mistakes

  • Prioritizing only by volume and producing a lesson for a topic the next product release will change; check the release plan before approving.
  • Treating a bug ticket as a usage question and teaching the customer to work around a defect, which becomes content debt when the bug is fixed.
  • Measuring success by lesson views instead of the drop in tickets on the topic.
  • Writing the script with the internal feature name instead of the name shown on the customer's screen.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between choosing the topic and a draft ready for reviewfrom 5 to 8 business days to 1 to 2 business daysestimate based on the described routine
Tickets on the topic in the 90 days after the material is publisheda 20% to 40% reduction against the previous 90 days, measured per topicestimate based on the described routine
Match between flagged topics and topics actually in demand6 out of 8 in the calibration quarterestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Content queue, September/2026 cycle, base of 1,940 tickets and 410 topics (Jun to Aug).

1. Multi-level approval rules | 142 tickets + 19 topics | no lesson, no article | Pro and Enterprise plans | estimated support cost: 47 h in the quarter | proposal: 12-min lesson + article
2. Spreadsheet import with custom columns | 118 tickets + 11 topics | article exists, reviewed in 2024-11, outdated screen | proposal: update the article, no new lesson
3. Usage report per user | 96 tickets + 24 topics | no material | all plans | proposal: short article with 3 screenshots
4. External user invitation with restricted access | 71 tickets + 8 topics | lesson exists (4 min), 9 views in 6 months | proposal: review the title and position in the track before producing

Draft of topic 1 (excerpt): Objective: by the end, the administrator sets up a rule with two sequential approvers and tests it with a request. Prerequisite: Administrator profile. Script: midnight context (why two levels), 1:30 a.m. Settings > Approvals screen [screenshot A], 4 a.m. approver order and deadline for each step [doc: approvals.md, Deadlines section], 8 a.m. test with a sample request, 10:30 a.m. three common mistakes. Check question 1: what happens if the first approver does not respond within 48 hours?
